Carlos Alcaraz covered his modesty as he cruised into the fourth round of the US Open.

The Spaniard’s baggy sleeveless top has been raising eyebrows this week as it occasionally revealed a nipple during matches.

The sight even prompted former player-turned-pundit Genie Bouchard to post on social media: “Love you Carlos but we’ve got to put the nip away.”

open image in gallery Alcaraz wore a vest to cover his modesty at Flushing Meadows (Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP) ( AP )

So Alcaraz fixed his malfunctioning wardrobe by wearing a skin-tight vest underneath as he beat China’s Wu Yibing 6-3 6-4 6-1 in a two hours and 19 minutes.

The 23-year-old, back to defend his title after four months out with a wrist injury, said he has surprised himself with how well he is playing.

“I think today was a really high rhythm, the way he played was unbelievable,” he said.

“I played aggressive, I played smart in the toughest moments which I’m really happy about. I did everything good. Could be better, but I’m proud of the performance today.

“To be honest I’m better than I thought. I thought I would be dead after the first match, but I’m recovering really well. Right now my level is really good.”

In the fourth round Alcaraz will play American Tommy Paul, the former Queen’s Club champion, who came through a titanic five-setter with Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik.

“He’s going to play at home which is going to be an advantage for him,” added Alcaraz. “But hopefully he will be a bit tired from today’s match.”

Russian seventh seed Daniil Medvedev beat France’s Arthur Rinderknech 6-4 6-4 6-4 while, in the women’s draw, third-seeded American Jessica Pegula recovered from a disastrous first set to knock out former runner-up Leylah Fernandez 1-6 6-4 6-3.

News.title: Liverpool cruise to victory at Ipswich after quick-fire Isak double
News.content:
There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

News.title: Forced displacement in the West Bank could be ‘crime against humanity’, says UN report
News.content:
Israel’s forced displacement of more than 33,000 Palestinians in the West Bank could amount to a “crime against humanity” and involves “ethnic cleansing”, according to a report published by the UN.

A report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) said that Israeli actions in the area had sparked the “largest and longest displacement crisis in the West Bank since 1967” – the year in which Israel captured the territory.

The report said “large-scale, long-term and systematic displacement of over 33,000 Palestinians from refugee camps … during Israel’s Operation Iron Wall [which] raises serious concerns of the crime against humanity of forcible transfer”.

It added: “The documented use of airstrikes, armoured bulldozers and controlled detonations, to render entire camps uninhabitable, to force the displacement of their residents and to prevent their return, in the absence of imperative military necessity to justify such destruction and displacement, are not permissible under international law, appear to amount to collective punishment and raise concerns of ethnic cleansing.”

The 27-page report covers the period December 5, 2024 to January 31, 2026.

In January 2025, Israeli forces launched “Operation Iron Wall” in the northern West Bank in a bid to counter what they said were terrorist threats.

They destroyed hundreds of homes, cut off water and electricity, and barred humanitarian access to the Jenin, Nur Sham and Tulkarm refugee camps.

By October 2025, 52 per cent of structures in Jenin camp, 48 per cent in Nur Shams and 36 percent in Tulkarm had been destroyed or damaged.

The three camps are among 19 in the West Bank established to shelter Palestinians after the 1948 Nakba, and are administered by the UN Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA).

Although still referred to as refugee camps, they are in fact now densely packed towns.

News.title: When is Black Friday 2026? This year’s dates and what to expect
News.content:
Five tips for finding genuine Black Friday discounts and deals

Learning how to find the best Black Friday discounts can make a meaningful difference to your festive budget, especially if you’re a keen sale shopper. The following five tips are a good starting point.

1. Don’t over-fixate on Black Friday itself

Although the day of Black Friday brings some of the best discounts of the festive sale season, good deals are likely to be available both before and after it – and some items may sell out.

“When we look at our pricing data on a daily level, you have certain events such as Amazon’s October Prime sale [not yet confirmed for 2026] that are an earlier vector for change in prices,” says Vivek Pandya, a director at Adobe for Business.

“We typically see more significant discounts starting to emerge as we get into late October or early November, and these really kick up a notch as we get into Black Friday week.”

So, while interest in Black Friday deals will peak around the day itself, some of the best deals may have been available since the beginning of the week, or earlier.

2. Expand your search to everyday essentials

At Telegraph Recommended, we’ve picked up on a proliferation of discounts on everyday household items during recent Black Friday sales (and during other occasional events such as Prime Day). If you need a top-up of items such as cleaning products or pet supplies, this could be a thrifty time to buy them.

“These sales have become a spending spree on what retailers frame as ‘everyday essentials’, as well as bigger items and gifts,” says Pandya. Last year’s Cyber Weekend saw a 260 per cent spike in sales of “personal care” items including cosmetics, shampoos, fragrances and toothbrushes, according to Adobe.

3. Use a price tracker

Free price tracking tools such as camelcamelcamel can show you how the price of a product has changed over time. This allows you to identify when a Black Friday deal has actually brought a product’s price significantly lower than usual, or when the retailer’s pricing strategy has artificially made a deal appear to be generous.

Gabrielė Vitkė, product marketing team lead at data-gathering specialist Decodo, warns shoppers to watch out for “anchoring”, where a product’s price is set high prior to Black Friday, allowing the retailer then to reduce it sharply and advertise an eye-catching reduction.

“Discounts on items such as electronics and computing products can seem steep, sometimes exceeding 50 per cent against the list price,” says Vitkė. “However, our data shows that prices in this category rose in the run-up to Black Friday 2025, which is a sign of anchor pricing before the ‘discount’ is applied.”

News.title: Indonesia wildfires trigger 50,000 respiratory infections
News.content:
More than 50,000 people have contracted respiratory infections in Indonesia, as raging wild fires blanket huge swathes of the country in a thick, toxic smoke.

The vast archipelago is only a month into its fire season, but intense blazes have proven hard to control across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo. There are fears the situation will only get worse, because the “Godzilla” El Niño is set to suppress rains that would normally have helped extinguish the flames.

“Our problems are not over. September is the peak of El Niño,” said Raja Juli Antoni, the forestry minister. “September is the main fight for us.”

Already the toxic haze has spread across Southeast Asia. On Friday Kuching, a city in Malaysian Borneo, was the most polluted city in the world on the IQ Air Index, followed by Jakarta and Singapore.

The wildfires have brought memories of record-breaking blazes in 2015. Then, the smoke was linked to roughly 100,000 excess deaths in Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore, according to one study. The World Bank said Indonesia alone saw economic losses of $16.1bn, or 2 per cent of GDP.

News.title: Global hunger is a threat to Britain’s national security, report says
News.content:
Global hunger poses a direct threat to Britain’s national security, and tackling it should be a government priority, a new report from the London School of Economics has warned.

It says hunger is a major driver of mass migration, extreme violence and war – events that threaten significant repercussions for Britain and Europe’s national security.

“Hunger prevention is an important part of national security policy, not an optional act of charity,” Stuart Gordon, professor of International Development at LSE and author of the report, told The Telegraph.

Recent hunger crises in places like Sudan, Afghanistan and across North Africa have contributed significantly to rising numbers of people moving to the West.

Between January and November 2025 alone, 12,684 migrants from Sudan – which is facing what has been described as the worst hunger crisis in Africa’s history – arrived in Europe, roughly three times as many as the previous year.

Last year, an estimated 155,000 African refugees arrived in Europe.

“Food insecurity tests one of the most basic expectations people have of government: that it will protect access to the essentials of life,” said Prof Gordon.

“Food price shocks can rapidly escalate into political instability when governments are perceived to have failed to protect access to basic subsistence goods,” he added.

News.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak slows at epicentre but widens elsewhere, modelling suggests
News.content:
Congo’s Ebola outbreak shows signs of slowing at the epicentre of the flare-up, but is widening as the infection spreads further afield, modelling suggests.

The daily tally of new cases in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) was falling at the end of August, but more cases were being found outside Ituri province, where the infection burst out.

Latest official figures say the outbreak has now killed more than 3,000 people out of over 6,100 confirmed cases, with the infection spreading faster than any previous epidemic of the viral haemorrhagic fever.

Modelling by Airfinity, a health analytics firm, suggests the true toll of cases could be more than four times higher than reported.

The outbreak remains on track to eclipse the 2014 West Africa outbreak later this month, to become the largest ever recorded.

Airfinity said that data from late August showed the seven-day averages of reported cases and reported deaths had fallen by 16 per cent and 18 per cent respectively.

The firm said it was “too early to confirm the decline will hold, and it may mask subnational variation: The outbreak has fluctuated before and a week of falling case and death counts does not rule out another surge.

“Even if the decline continues at this current pace, low case levels remain weeks away.”

News.title: Bank of England must raise interest rates, says chief economist
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Government borrowing costs edged lower on Thursday as Andy Burnham continues to face scrutiny over the public finances.

The yield on 10-year US treasury bonds – considered a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money – declined slightly to 4.78pc on Thursday after a drop in oil prices.

Pre-market trading of bonds in Britain, France and Germany suggested the market was poised to rally after a brutal first half of the week.

However, Mr Burnham and Chancellor John Healey remain under intense pressure, with analysts estimating that as much as half of the country’s fiscal headroom has been wiped out by the jump in bond yields.

Borrowing costs surged after a jump in oil prices caused by fresh strikes between the US and Iran.

The yield on 10-year gilts, as UK bonds are known, hit levels not seen since the global financial crisis in 2007, while longer-term debt costs hit their highest point since 1998.

It means the Chancellor will have less room for manoeuvre in the Budget next month, with some economists predicting the rise in borrowing costs has wiped out up to £14bn of breathing room.

The rise in bond yields across major economies had deepened concerns about deteriorating financial conditions.

Central banks in the US and Europe are increasingly expected to raise interest rates this month to combat inflation caused by the Iran war, although the Bank of England is expected to hold rates steady for now.

Gavin Friend, an analyst at NAB, said: “If this war ‌were to be ‌put to bed, then that ⁠would certainly be something very positive to bring yields back down again across the board.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

What happened overnight

Oil prices slipped, helping boost stocks and bonds.

Renewed fighting between the US and Iran pushed oil prices sharply higher earlier in the week.

However, Brent crude was trading near $94 a barrel after Donald Trump said he does not expect the US bombing campaign to last “much longer”.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 advanced 0.2pc to 64,455.83. Among major gainers, OpenAI investor SoftBank Group rose 2.9pc, memory chipmaker Kioxia rose 0.6pc, and chip equipment manufacturer Tokyo Electron gained 0.8pc.

South Korea’s Kospi rose 1.4pc to 6,656.81. Samsung was 1.3pc higher, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix was up 1.4pc.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng edged 0.1pc higher, to 25,344.80. The Shanghai Composite index climbed 0.4pc to 3,958.79.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.5pc to 9,025.10.

The Taiex in Taiwan rose 0.6pc, while India’s Sensex climbed 0.3pc.

It comes after Wall Street bounced back after its sharp sell-off at the start of September, as investors snapped up shares that had fallen in recent days.

The S&P 500 rose, with almost 350 companies ending higher. Dell was among the biggest winners, jumping 14pc after giving an upbeat outlook, while investors were also looking ahead to results from chipmaker Broadcom.

The recovery came despite continued concerns over inflation, with oil prices remaining high as fighting between the US and Iran escalated. Brent crude briefly climbed close to $97 a barrel before easing back after Donald Trump said he did not expect the renewed bombing campaign to last “too long”.

US government bond yields were little changed after surging to their highest levels in several years earlier in the week.

Investors also got a mixed picture from the Federal Reserve’s latest assessment of the US economy. Economic activity increased modestly over the past two months, helped by strong demand from data centres, while companies added jobs at a slower pace in August.

The figures come ahead of Friday’s closely watched US jobs report, which could influence expectations for the next move in interest rates.

News.title: Weapons and mercenaries from foreign states fuelling Sudan’s war, UN report finds
News.content:
The war in Sudan is being fuelled by weapons and mercenaries from external states including the United Arab Emirates, Colombia and Turkey, a United Nations report has found.

An investigation by a UN fact-finding mission published on Thursday found that the supply of drones in particular to both sides in the civil war was extending the fighting’s reach and contributing to war crimes.

“Increasingly sophisticated drone capabilities [has] enabled both parties to strike far beyond immediate front lines”, says the report.

“The [UN] mission calls on States to enforce the Darfur arms embargo and suspend transfers of weapons, drones, components, or military assistance where there is a substantial risk of their use in serious violations”.

Sudan’s civil war erupted in April 2023 following a power struggle between the head of the military and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as part of a planned transition to civilian rule. Hundreds of thousands have died and some 14 million people have been displaced in what has become the world’s deadliest conflict.

In a previous report in February, following the capture of El Fasher in which at least 60,000 people were killed, the UN said the RSF’s mass killings of Black African ethnic groups, including Zaghawa and Fur, bore the “hallmarks of genocide”.

The latest report said “individuals and entities” in the UAE were part of a transnational network supplying weapons, logistics, training and foreign personnel to the RSF – including NORINCO AH-4 howitzers, FK-20000 air defence systems and Chinese-made CH-95 strike drones.

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), meanwhile, separately obtained Turkish-manufactured drones, including Bayraktar Akıncı combat drones and Yiha III loitering munitions.

The Turkish embassy in London has been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Football’s lack of patience extraordinary… even legendary Sir Alex Ferguson probably wouldn’t have survived at Man Utd
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL has developed an extraordinary lack of patience.

We want a new manager but we want results immediately.



We want that young player but only if he looks like a £100million footballer by Christmas.

We want a new signing to justify his price tag before he properly unpacks his suitcase.



We want a club to build for the future but also want to know why they haven’t won today.

I have spent more than 30 years in football and sat in boardrooms when results have been poor.

The atmosphere changes. Questions get louder. Everyone wants to know what is going to be done.

Sometimes the hardest decision is not to do something. It is to resist doing something simply because everyone else wants you to.

At West Ham, there were spells when fans demanded David Moyes be sacked. Results weren’t good enough and pressure mounted.

But we didn’t sack him. We stayed with him. And in 2023, West Ham won the Conference League — a first European trophy in 58 years.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That doesn’t mean keeping a manager is always right. But that decision should be made with your head, not because the football world is shouting at you.

And that brings me to Sir Alex Ferguson. Would he have survived at Manchester United in the modern game?

United finished 11th in his first season after he took over in November 1986. They were second the next campaign but dropped back to 11th in 1988-89. His first trophy came in 1990.

Imagine that happening now. There would be TV panels asking if he had lost the dressing room. Social media would be demanding his dismissal.

United might have sacked one of the greatest managers in history before he had a chance to become one. And that is the danger of impatience. It affects players too.



A young star has three bad games and suddenly is a flop. A £60m signing doesn’t score in four matches and suddenly the transfer is a disaster.

Football is different from almost every other business. All our assets are people — the players, manager and staff are the business.

When your assets are people, your job isn’t simply to measure them, replace them and move on.

It is to lead them, support them, develop them and give them the confidence to perform at their best.

People rarely shine at work when they are constantly waiting to be judged, blamed or replaced.



Sacking is expensive

Sometimes the most valuable thing a board can give a manager is time, trust and confidence.

Constant change is expensive too. Sack a manager and you pay off him and his staff. Bring in another and he may want different players. Those signings cost money.

Then another manager arrives and doesn’t fancy half of them. That isn’t ambition. Sometimes it is simply expensive indecision.

We talk endlessly about long-term projects — building a culture, developing young players, creating a clear identity… Then give the manager five games.

I am not saying managers should have unlimited time. I’ve been involved in decisions where it was clear a boss had run his course.



But sacking someone is the easy part. Finding a better replacement is the hard part.

Owners need the courage to stick to a plan when they genuinely believe it is right.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And those commenting on football should be careful about turning every bad result into a crisis.

Football is not a television series where every episode needs a cliffhanger.

Sometimes the boring decision is the sensible one.

Sports.title: Gus Poyet warns Tosin Adarabioyo to brace himself for Chelsea boos after following his footsteps by joining Tottenham
Sports.content:
TOSIN ADARABIOYO is the first player since Gus Poyet to move from Chelsea to Tottenham in a paid transfer since May 2001.

The £8million deadline day signing of Tosin, 28, ended a 25-year streak of Tottenham not paying any money for a Chelsea player, with a large part of that marked by a rivalry between former club owners Daniel Levy and Roman Abramovich.



In fact, the only business done in that period between the clubs at all, was a free transfer for Carlo Cudicini, Chelsea buying goalkeeper Neil Sullivan for £500,000 as Cudicini’s backup, and young striker Jude Soonsup-Bell moving to Spurs’ youth team from Chelsea’s academy.

And while the Uruguayan midfielder is regarded as a cult hero at Stamford Bridge for his finest moments, he was not always so highly thought of by Blues fans after making the switch in 2001.



But in an exclusive interview with SunSport, on behalf of Gambling.com, Poyet revealed how “naive” he was about his move, and sent a warning to Tosin over the reception he might get when he returns to Stamford Bridge.

He said: “I think I was a little bit naive – I didn’t realise the impact it would have on Chelsea supporters until after I signed for Spurs.

“When I was at Chelsea and we were trying to win trophies, the goal was to win the Premier League, and to do that we needed to beat Man United or Arsenal.

“To me we did not respect Spurs, they were not our biggest rivals, that’s the bottom line.”

Poyet, 58, also admitted that he was forced away from the club he loved by former manager Claudio Ranieri.

And in a sense, Tosin may feel the same way about Xabi Alonso, having been left surplus to requirements this season.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The defender posted an emotional message to Chelsea fans on social media after he left, which was largely well received by Blues supporters, most of whom are more than pleased with the £8m fee that the club received for him.

Some have even suggested that his name will be cheered when it is read out by the Chelsea stadium announcer.

The reality is, there will likely be boos for him.

Perhaps less of a hostile reception for Mykhailo Mudryk who also joined the North London club on deadline day, though he joined on loan with a desperation to get his Premier League career back on track following his suspension.



Poyet insisted that players sometimes have to make tough decisions like that and take their personal lives into account, and joked it’s not surprising anymore, given how much Spurs have spent in this window.

He added: “In my head, going to Spurs was normal, it would be worse to go to United or Arsenal, so when Ranieri started getting rid of the strong heads like me and Dennis Wise, I had to make a decision.”

“It was only after I signed and saw the reactions that I realised what I’d done. It was strange. I was naive.

“You also need to understand though how a player feels about Chelsea. I remember how I felt, I was in love with Chelsea and that was no secret, they are my team, but they didn’t want me and that was upsetting, I needed to live.



“You expect me to go to a worse club, for less money which was worse for my family, just so that I didn’t upset anyone? What about me?

“I couldn’t stay at Chelsea, the manager wanted to do everything differently to me, and they spent £100m and didn’t win a trophy, and I had to go somewhere else.

“Glenn Hoddle came to my house and showed me the project and showed my wife, so it’s a bit unfair sometimes – you need to know how the coaches are making the players feel – some coaches that will say to a player “you’re not wanted here and you need to go” and as a player that feels unfair.”



Poyet did have some defending of Tosin and Mudryk to do after his naivety 25 years ago, and gave them some grace that it could be worse.

They could have gone from Arsenal to Tottenham, or vice-versa.

The midfielder feels that the rivalry between Spurs and the Blues is one that is manufactured, and not a ‘proper’ derby like that in North London.

“Chelsea and Tottenham for me, is not realistically a derby.

“The only derby in London is Arsenal vs Spurs, the rest are London derbies that are the equivalent to a derby in Sussex or Derby – you can’t tell me that Chelsea vs Tottenham and Arsenal vs Tottenham is the same level, I played in both.

“Chelsea needed a derby because Fulham, West Ham and Crystal Palace were not rivals to them for various reasons, but the derby in London is Tottenham vs Arsenal and nothing else.”

Poyet was speaking exclusively to SunSport on behalf of Gambling.com.

Sports.title: Insider on Jamie Vardy’s show lifts lid on what crew really thought of Mike Dean’s controversial ‘mini-games’ rant
Sports.content:
MIKE DEAN left crew members on Jamie Vardy’s podcast stunned after revealing he played “games” while refereeing Premier League matches.

The ex-official, 58, sent shockwaves through football after reflecting on his career.



And furious Premier League sides have launched internal probes following Dean’s claims on Jamie Vardy’s Having a Party.

His revelations included going as long as possible without blowing his whistle and staying camped in the centre circle during showdowns.



Dean surprised Vardy and those working behind the scenes when he made the admission while the cameras were rolling.

A show insider exclusively told SunSport: “We didn’t think he was being serious.

“It felt like he just wanted to be one of the lads and say some funny stuff. It felt like he wanted to have a bit of banter to be one of the lads.”

Dean has come under fire since admitting he used to amuse himself in the middle of Premier League clashes.

Speaking to former England striker Vardy, the ex-ref – who became a dedicated VAR official after hanging up his whistle in 2022 – said: “There used to be games we’d have, as a laugh.

“We used to say, ‘we’ll kick-off now, right, see how long we can go without blowing a whistle’.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“I done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously. Went 20, 25 minutes without blowing a whistle. Few times… let it go, let it go, let it go.”

Dean added: “I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave.

“That was just me, joking about. The lads that used to be on the line would say ‘you can’t’. I got to about 15 minutes once, in one game.”

Dean hit back at suggestions the games clouded his judgement on the pitch by releasing a statement.

It read: “Throughout my 25 years as a professional referee, I have always applied the laws of the game to the best of my ability.



“My approach as a referee was always to allow the game to flow and whenever possible I preferred to apply a high threshold for contact which the players liked.

“However, if I saw a foul challenge that needed me to take the appropriate action I would give it from the correct position.

“At no stage was it my intention to question, criticise or undermine the integrity of refereeing in this country.



“I have always respected the profession and the responsibility that comes with being a referee.”

SunSport understands officiating chiefs at Pro Ref are deeply sceptical of Dean’s shock claims.

But his comments resulted in shock, anger and disbelief among those in charge.

Pro Ref does not believe there is anything to back up the admission, with some convinced Dean was simply playing to the audience.

Fellow ex-Premier League ref Graham Scott described Dean’s claims as “dispiriting clickbait”.

But with a full pre-season behind him the Swede has hit the ground running this year.

A second said: “If he stays fit he’s scoring a guaranteed 25 league goals.”

A third added: “We robbed Newcastle.”

Another said: “WHAT A HIT FROM ISAK, FAIRS MAN HE MIGHT JUST BE BACK.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Isak put the ball in the net for a third time in the 33rd minute, but the goal was ruled out for offside.

Curiously, all of Isak’s goals so far this season have been assisted by Cody Gakpo, who seemed destined to leave Anfield for most of the summer amid interest from Tottenham and Manchester City.

How different this season could have started for Liverpool and Isak if Gakpo had not been around…

Sports.title: Over £300million on transfers, 54 comings & goings, no points, no goals, no clear plan… Tottenham have nowhere to hide
Sports.content:
MORE than £300million spent, 54 comings and goings, no points, no goals and no clear plan.

After all the early summer optimism, Tottenham look like a bit of a mess once again.



If you are struggling to decide whether Spurs have had a brilliant transfer window or simply thrown heaps of money at a problem, there is an easy solution.

Deadline day finished with them signing Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhailo Mudryk from Chelsea.



And would that have been in any master plan? Of course not.

Tosin gets a bit of flak for being signed largely for his personality but he has had a great career.

Though his arrival still does not inspire much, especially given that Spurs have lost Cristian Romero.

Hundreds of millions have been spent but no one can still answer the simple question of who is going to score Tottenham ten goals this season?

To fork out that much money, on that many players, and not be able to confidently state someone will hit that number is troubling.

All the talk around Roberto De Zerbi’s side is how good they could be if everyone is available and in form — never a good place to be at that cost.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It is just like when they had Ledley King at the back.

Everyone would wonder just how good it would be when they could get 20 games a season out of the defender at least.

Now De Zerbi is looking after a squad where around half of the players are in that same King boat.

The picture is not good after a messy end to the summer. There was a long chase for Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye was all but done before, somehow, ending up at Manchester City.

Ndiaye would have been a great addition. I played against him when he was at Sheffield United and he always stood out.



The move to Manchester is his biggest jump, so there will still be questions.

But he is a very brave player and on a whole different level to Mudryk.

Spurs have gone from nearly landing either Gakpo or Ndiaye to now having to sit back and watch City and Liverpool – who have since added Bradley Barcola – become stronger.



Opponents appear stronger and, because of that whole mess, Richarlison is still at Spurs and absolutely raging.

My former team-mate has always been a character but De Zerbi has said he only wanted players around the place as long as they were fully committed.

Richarlison being left out of the Premier League squad certainly underlined that.

Mudryk is a whole different story. He may have done well under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, but that was some years ago now.

And, as we all know, he has been banned for the past 18 months.



That isn’t just missing games due to injury or a crisis of form, he has not even been able to train with Chelsea’s squad. All alone for almost two years.

We can see he is rapid and in great physical shape – he clearly looks after himself – but the Ukrainian has not been getting any reps in when it comes to being match-ready.

The concern isn’t that he won’t be able to hack it in matches, just training day in, day out could be a struggle.



Tottenham’s big bet is that De Zerbi, who touted him as a future Ballon d’Or winner, can return Mudryk to his pre-ban best. It is quite the gamble.

That is not the only thing they have risked on the Italian. De Zerbi made big requests this summer in terms of spending and they have all been delivered.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There is nowhere for him to hide. You can’t blame the ownership as Daniel Levy is not there now. You can’t blame the lack of spending.

They are not going to blame the players as you ultimately need them to perform. So the only person who is liable to get the chop is the manager.

Sports.title: Why does new Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola wear the number 29 shirt?
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL unveiled their marquee signing of the summer earlier this week in Bradley Barcola from PSG, but fans are wondering why the Frenchman wears an unusual shirt number.

After winning back-to-back Champions League titles in the French capital, Barcola has left Luis Enrique’s side for a dizzying fee of £123million.



The winger is the third most expensive signing in Premier League history behind teammate Alexander Isak and Manchester City’s deadline day signing of Enzo Fernandez, who were both bought for £125million.

The transfer took Liverpool‘s summer spending up to £224million, of which £219million is net spend.



Barcola joins a frontline alongside Isak, Cody Gakpo and fellow new-boy Victor Munoz, who was signed from Osasuna for £34.5million – the Spaniard scored his first goal for the Reds in a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest.

On his unveiling, Barcola was wearing the unusual number 29 shirt, and SunSport has all the information on why.

Why does new Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola wear the number 29 shirt?

Despite having a number of conventional shirt numbers to choose from, including Mohamed Salah‘s 11 shirt, Barcola has opted to wear the number 29.

He donned the same number at PSG, and there is a bizarre reason as to why he wears it, stemming from his love for Fifa (now EA FC) video game franchise.

Specifically, it was the series’ “the journey” story mode, featuring fictional rising star Alex Hunter, that left a mark on the Frenchman.

Barcola previously explained: “When I was younger, I used to play FIFA. In the story mode with Alex Hunter, this number became symbolic for me.



“I thought to myself: ‘The day I go pro, it’ll be number 29.’ And here I am, I adopted it, and now I’ll never let it go.”

Previous No29s at Anfield include Fabio Borini and Dominic Solanke, but it has been vacant since Arthur Melo left the club during the 2022/23 season.

Sports.content:
Desperate Everton turn to Jamie Vardy and ex-Man Utd star after deadline day farce

Former Leicester City and England star Jamie Vardy has been without a club since leaving Italian side Cremonese at the end of last season but he could potentially be back in the Premier League

View 2 Images Jamie Vardy could be an emergency option for Everton (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Vardy is being ‘considered’ by Everton following their disastrous summer transfer window. The Toffees had a dismal end to their window under David Moyes, having sold Beto to Fiorentina.

Everton attempted to add to their attacking options with a move for Monaco’s Folarin Balogun but that deal fell through at the last minute. They also failed to get a move over the line for Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City.

That leaves Everton with just Thierno Barry as their only central attacking option. But the Merseysiders could potentially look into the free agent market to add to their squad.

According to The Sun, Everton are considering a move for Vardy, who is without a club since leaving Italian side Cremonese in the summer. The veteran forward, now 39, scored seven goals in 29 appearances in Serie A following a glittering spell with Leicester.

He netted 200 goals in 500 outings for the Foxes, helping them to the Premier League, FA Cup and three seasons in Europe. Vardy has been linked with a number of clubs this summer, with Wrexham, West Ham and Sheffield Wednesday all mentioned as potential destinations.

Vardy is not the only free agent being considered by Everton after deadline day. talkSPORT have reported that they have also been offered the services of former Man United star Anthony Martial.

The French forward is currently without a club following a brief spell with Mexican side Monterrey. He has also played for Greek side AEK Athens following his exit from Old Trafford.

“We lost Illy (Iliman Ndiaye), someone we definitely didn’t want to lose. But sometimes it’s quite difficult when the likes of Man City come along looking for your players.

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool winger Jordon Ibe spared jail after assaulting ex in 'druggy' row
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool winger Jordon Ibe spared jail after assaulting ex in 'druggy' row

Jordon Ibe admitted assaulting his ex-girlfriend after pulling a braid from her head - the footballer played 58 times for Liverpool and had spells at Derby County, Birmingham City and AFC Bournemouth

View 2 Images Jordon Ibe played 58 times for Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

A former Liverpool winger has been spared jail after assaulting his ex-girlfriend.

‌



Jordon Ibe, 30, pulled a braid out of ex-girlfriend’s Amie Mayson head during an argument outside her home in Lambeth, south London.

‌



Croydon Magistrates’ Court heard Ibe and Ms Mayson were arguing on December 14 when Ms Mayson confronted Ibe and demanded he repaid her money she said he owed her. After Ms Mayson asked to be reimbursed, Ibe told her: “No, I’m going to be a pr*ck.”

‌



Prosecutors said Ibe had a bag containing drinks, snacks and flowers, but when Ms Mayson threw muffins on the floor and called Ibe a “druggy”, he grabbed her by her hair. Ibe left Ms Mayson with a bald patch after pulling the braid, the court was told.

The footballer made 58 appearances for Liverpool and had spells at Derby County and Birmingham City in the Championship, before playing for AFC Bournemouth in the Premier League.

View 2 Images Jordon Ibe training with Bournemouth in 2019 (Image: Photo by Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

‌



The former England under-21 international had been playing non-league football in recent years before moving to Lokomotiv Sofia in the Bulgarian First League in 2025.

On Friday, magistrate Brij Kalia sentenced Ibe to a 12-month community order, 80 hours of unpaid work and 27 days of rehabilitation activity. Ibe was also handed a £764 fine, including £114 of surcharge and £650 in court costs.

Ibe, who represented himself at the hearing wearing a black coat and black trousers, told the court: “I made a serious mistake.”

‌



He added: “I understand it is wrong. I am genuinely remorseful. I’ve had to look at myself in the mirror. I cannot change what I did but will take responsibility for what I do next.”

Ms Alshekhili said the attack left Ms Mayson’s confidence, self-esteem and self-worth “on the floor”. In a victim impact statement read to the court, Ms Mayson said: “I want the court to understand the impact that this incident has had... The assault has had a significant impact on me both physically and mentally.”

She said despite remaining “feelings of fear”, she felt “compassion” for Ibe, adding forgiveness had been part of her “healing journey”.

Article continues below

Ibe, of Chislehurst, south-east London, pleaded guilty to the charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm in July, after denying it in March.

On Friday, Ms Alshekhili said that prior to the assault the pair had been on an “on and off” relationship since late 2024.

Roy Keane's £25m son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis dealt crushing Aston Villa blow

‌



Due to only having two “club-trained” players, Villa are only permitted to name a 23-man 'A list' squad rather than the usual 25 limit. And Harwood-Bellis is one of the unlucky ones who has failed to make the cut.

He is the only summer signing not to be registered, with Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Leon Goretzka, Joao Gomes, Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Alejandro Garnacho and Ibahim Mbaye all in the squad.

‌



Harwood-Bellis' move to Villa Park descended into a bit of a saga during the final weeks of the window with Villa initially failing to meet Southampton's valuation for the defender, who represented England back in 2024. The Saints were almost promoted to the Premier League themselves last season, reaching the final of the Championship play-offs before being expelled over 'Spygate'.

Roy Keane, Harwood-Bellis' father-in-law, alluded to some of the difficulties of the situation behind the scenes and lauded the former Saints player's professionalism during the situation, telling the The Overlap: “He is a lot more professional than I was.

“He does not speak to me much about it. I have boundaries with him and I won’t be interfering with his business. Every now and again you might just give a bit of advice but not I would not be overbearing. He has his own stuff to do.”

The former Manchester United and Ireland midfielder added: “That last year as [Southampton] were kicked out of the play-offs I think Villa is a great move for him.”

Sports.title: Mike Dean is an attention seeker who can't be taken seriously - his claims are nonsense
Sports.content:
Mike Dean is an attention seeker who can't be taken seriously - his claims are nonsense

OPINION: Mike Dean is an entertaining pundit but his stories are not believable - and cause current referees a major issue

View 2 Images Mike Dean's recent claims have left the football world bemused (Image: YouTube/Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast)

Mike Dean probably feels like he does not owe the refereeing fraternity anything.

‌



Which is probably a good thing because, yet again, another bizarre outburst has done more damage to officials and the way fans view referees.

‌



Dean’s assertion that he would set himself mini-challenges during matches “as a laugh” has certainly caught the headlines. Appearing on Jamie Vardy’s podcast, Dean says he would try to go “20, 25 minutes without blowing a whistle.”

‌



"I used to do another thing. I used to stand in the centre circle - see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The problem here is that, whether they like it or not, the average fan already has a bit of a downer on referees. And the natural inclination is to think all referees are the same.

‌



Obviously they are not. We boast some excellent officials in the Premier League. Honest! But there will be fans up and down the country this weekend, watching the game, looking cynically at the referee and saying to the person next to them: “Yeah, did you see what Mike Dean said?”

That’s the problem. I actually think Dean might be better in the media than he was as a referee. He is entertaining. When he’s on Sky, he buys into the jokes in the studio. He’s got something to say.

View 2 Images Dean retired in 2022 (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

‌



But he is clearly looking for headlines and attention. And therefore, can you take him seriously as a serious pundit? I’m not sure you can. You can have him on for comedy value. But let’s not pretend he’s a serious voice of authority. He’s not anymore.

He is just looking to make a splash for attention. What he has said about not whistling for 25 minutes is just utter nonsense. Watch a game this weekend. They blow all the time.

Standing in the centre circle? Don’t be so ridiculous. Former referees - and it is quite a cliquey business - think it’s the most ridiculous and unbelievable thing they’ve ever heard.

‌



It’s nonsense but does quite well for a podcast. Certainly drives interest! Mind you, as a pal pointed out… not even Jamie Vardy thought it was funny.

Jason Cundy rips into 'liar' Mike Dean in explosive rant live on talkSPORT READ MORE :

Dean is a guy who loves the attention. He had so many clashes with Premier League managers. My most memorable was his war of words with Arsene Wenger after a 1-1 draw at West Brom in 2018.

Listen, a referee should be treated with respect. Managers overstep the mark. But it felt obvious that Dean wanted to be the centre of attention. Afterwards, Wenger talked about how hard he and David Dein had fought to make refs professional. And here we are…

‌



Back in August 2022, Dean was on VAR when he did not send referee Anthony Taylor to the screen to review Cristian Romero’s hair pull on Marc Cucurella. It was an obvious mistake. The reasoning? He did not want to cause Taylor more trouble after a feisty game.

Sadly, we can’t take Dean seriously anymore. He is entertaining. But unfortunately the quips do damage to serious officials. And that’s the wider problem.

Sports.title: Jason Cundy rips into 'liar' Mike Dean in explosive rant live on talkSPORT
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy rips into 'liar' Mike Dean in explosive rant live on talkSPORT

Mike Dean has been storytelling about his time refereeing in the Premier League, but former Chelsea midfielder Jason Cundy is skeptical to saw the least

View 3 Images Jason Cundy has torn into Mike Dean (Image: X/talkSPORT)

Former Chelsea midfielder Jason Cundy has accused ex-Premier League referee Mike Dean of "lying" about the games he claims he played while refereeing. Dean, who retired as an official in 2022, has been a regular on Sky Sports as an analyst.

‌



However, he has also made many appearances on podcasts in his spare time. His latest one caused a stir, as he claimed to take part in mischievous, inside games while overseeing matches, including staying within the centre circle for as long as possible and seeing how long he could go without blowing his whistle for a foul.

‌



Mirror readers have even called for the FA to investigate the 58-year-old. His stories have also left Cundy enraged, as he feels the former referee has not only been untruthful, but has also given supporters a reason to mistrust officials who are currently working in the game.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Speaking on talkSPORT, Cundy, when asked about Dean's tale, said: "Liar. He’s a liar. I don’t believe a word that’s come out of his mouth. You cannot stand as a referee for 15 minutes in the centre circle. He’d get done.

"He’s lying to everyone. I don’t know why he is doing it. I don’t believe him. I heard this earlier, that one (staying within the centre circle for as long as possible), is absolute rubbish. That’s easy to find out.

‌



"Go to every game that he refereed in the Premier League. It’s rubbish, he’s a liar. The other one when he was waving ‘Play on, play on’ for 20 minutes. I don’t know what’s going on inside his head, but that’s absolute BS.”

View 3 Images Mike Dean's recent claims have left the football world bemused (Image: YouTube/Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast)

Cundy also believes Dean's stories have also piled the pressure on current officials, who are already being scrutinised and abused by current supporters who feel disgruntled about their decisions.

‌



The ex-defender added: "All you are doing is making the referees who have followed your path, where every single referee and every single decision is scrutinised, and he’s sat there with his legs crossed laughing and joking about something that is so important.

"Let’s say he’s right and he stayed in the centre circle for 15 minutes. How is that helping the future generation of referees in the Premier League? We know as fans how critical we are of refs.

View 3 Images Dean retired in 2022 (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

‌



"Now we have someone who is sitting there, smug, laughing, trying to make light of one of the most important jobs in football, every Saturday, when we follow our football club, and he’s making a joke about trying to stay in the football circle."

Ex-Premier League referee Graham Scott also believes Dean's claims were "nonsense" while ex-official Mark Helsey was also left in disbelief, telling BBC Sport: "All my years as a professional referee, I have to say I’ve never heard of these games. Never. And I have to say that I have never, ever thought about playing any sort of game, going out to referee.

"So I’m astounded, and if Mike has played these games, then he’s done that on his own accord. And if he has, then I think we need to know what games he’s done them in? How many games he’s done them in? And it brings into question the integrity of every official.”

Sports.title: Greaves makes more history with win at Czech Darts Open
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves made more darting history as she became the first woman to win a match on the PDC's European Tour - a feat that secured her a second-round clash with Luke Humphries at the Czech Darts Open.

The 22-year-old rallied from 3-1 down to beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in Prague on Friday night and will now play world No 2 Humphries in the last-32 on Saturday evening, with the winner meeting Nathan Aspinall or Andrew Gilding in round three on Sunday.

Greaves' latest landmark moment follows becoming the first woman to hit a nine-darter on the PDC Pro Tour, against Mensur Suljovic back in February, and the first to win a PDC ranking title, doing so when she edged Michael Smith 8-7 at Players Championship 11.

Image: Gurney had pipped Greaves in a first-round match at the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace (Pic credit: PDC)

She was also the first woman to qualify for a European Tour event when she reached last month's Hungarian Darts Trophy.

Greaves lost to Rob Cross in the first round in Budapest but her run in Prague will now last at least one more match after defeating Gurney, a player she had suffered a narrow 3-2 loss to in round one of the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace.

The Yorkshirewoman pinned double one to clinch victory over 'Superchin' in the Czech Republic.

Littler to begin campaign on Saturday

Elsewhere on Friday, Niko Springer routed Martin Homola 6-0 to book a second-round meeting with world No 1 Luke Littler, while Joe Cullen, Dirk van Duijvenbode and Cross were big-name casualties, dumped out by Stephen Burton, Mario Vandenbogaerde and Keane Barry respectively.

Humphries, who, like Littler, received a bye to round two as one of the 16 seeded players, has won the last two Czech Darts Open titles, thrashing Kim Huybrechets 8-1 in the 2024 final and then seeing off Josh Rock 8-5 last year.

'Cool Hand' is targeting a fourth victory in five years at this event having knocked off Rob Cross 8-5 in the 2022 final.

Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price are also in Prague and will take on Mario Vandenbogaerde and Callan Rydz respectively on Saturday night.

Sports.title: How influencers at US Open are testing boundaries of tennis etiquette
Sports.content:
A huge discussion around tennis etiquette has been sparked at the US Open due to the disruption caused by a growing number of content creators and influencers at Flushing Meadows.

The number of content creators who have been accredited to cover this year's final Grand Slam of the year has doubled from last year in a move by organisers to reach new audiences. Yet the noise and disturbance caused by them in the stands as been felt by players on court.

Chair umpire Kader Nouni admonished a group of influencers in a suite for recording a video in the middle of a point, while another incident saw a creator using the use of a bright portable ring light to take photos.

Meanwhile, in Naomi Osaka's second-round victory, chair umpire Marijana Veljovic asked fans several times to be quiet.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Naomi Broady and Ryan Harrison try to teach some UK influencers how to play tennis at the US Open

Some players have questioned whether the push for online engagement has gone too far with two-time champion Osaka saying: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.".

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette."

The US Open introduced a policy of free fan movement in 2024, meaning spectators no longer have to wait to take their seats during changeovers.

And since Osaka's opening match, there has been increased messaging on screens reminding people to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights.

Some of the behaviour 'disrespectful'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports tennis panel discusses the best fashion so far at the US Open

American and third seed Jessica Pegula has said some of the behaviour has been "disrespectful".

"I can appreciate the influencers coming and showcasing the US Open experience," she said. "But I do think that it's tough when you see videos when they're taking pictures and using the selfie lights.

"People are down there trying to perform. It's their career and their job. It seems a bit disrespectful."

Celebrities have long been ubiquitous in the stands - from A-list stars to US President Donald Trump - as the ultra-wealthy shell out thousands of dollars for seats to get through Flushing Meadows' doors.

But the growing love affair between influencers and the premier ⁠American tennis event has caused some growing pains.

World No 4 Coco Gauff welcomed the influx of new fans but said they should respect the traditions of tennis.

"I definitely think it's cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport," she said.

"But if you're being invited to a red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans.

"I think it's just follow the etiquette of the sport."

'We all want tennis to grow'

Eliza Wastcoat is an influencer who has a passion and knowledge for tennis. She has even launched her own social media channel exploring the intersection of tennis and fashion.

Wastcoat, who moved to America to attend the prestigious Lehigh University, and began her professional career at a creative agency, believes there is room to grow the game but only if organisers and influencers can work together.

"There is a space in tennis for influencers and content creators to be welcomed into the sport and reach new audiences, but I think there's ways in which the sport can do that which includes content creators and influencers who appreciate the sport itself and the etiquette of it and for those who are maybe new and are bringing new audiences in," said Wastcoat, who served as a Wimbledon ball kid when she was younger.

"I do think it's the responsibility of both the brands, the tournaments and the individuals coming to read up a little bit and understand the etiquette of the type of sporting event they're going to.

"Tennis has really opened up its doors to change but ultimately players need some quiet and the ability to concentrate.

"We all want tennis to grow so inviting people in and making it an all-round experience is great for the game, so it's just an opportunity to further educate people about the game on what tennis is."

A learning curve for the USTA

The United States Tennis Association said it wanted fans to have an "incredible time" while ensuring they did not interfere with the action.

"We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited," read a statement from the governing body.

Sports.title: Lawrence leads at halfway stage in Switzerland as he aims to emulate Ballesteros
Sports.content:
Defending champion Thriston Lawrence reeled off six birdies in a row and then made an excellent par save from a bunker to secure the lead at the halfway stage of the Omega European Masters as he looks to emulate the late, great Seve Ballesteros.

Ballesteros is the only player to win this event three times since it became a DP World Tour tournament in 1972, doing so in 1977, 1978 and 1989 - but Lawrence has a chance to do likewise having triumphed at Crans-sur-Siere in 2022 and then again last season.

The South African carded a bogey-free, seven-under 63 on Friday to reach 13 under par and take a two-shot advantage over Germany's Jeremy Paul and Spain's Ignacio Elvira - who shot a round-of-the day 62 - into the weekend in Switzerland.

Japan's Keita Nakajima sits fourth on 10 under with England's Paul Casey among a group of three players in a share of fifth on nine under with 36 holes remaining.

Casey's compatriot Harry Hall reached 10 under through nine holes of his second round after five front-nine birdies saw him go out in 30, only for a hip injury to then hamper him as he bogeyed three of his final five and slipped to seven under, six shots off the pace.

Image: Lawrence is a five-time winner on the DP World Tour, including twice at the Omega European Masters

Lawrence: I've been playing well all year

Starting at the 10th, Lawrence parred five of his first six holes around a birdie at 13 before he ignited from the 16th when a superb tee shot left him a tap-in birdie.

The 29-year-old picked up shots at his next five holes, too, with highlights including draining from over 40 feet at the first and then holing from off the green at the second.

Lawrence was unable to add to his birdie haul across the last third of his round but saved par at five when he chipped on from the sand - his second attempt to get out of that hazard having initially used the putter to no avail.

Lawrence, without a top-10 finish since March, said afterwards: "I've played well all year. I've just been unfortunate so many times, missing the cut by one shot four or five times. I feel like I've been playing well, but mentally, I'm in a much better space.

"Obviously, seeing birdies and seeing putts go in, I feel like you gain confidence from that. Coming back to a place I love is just extra confidence."

Sports.title: Star-studded London City cruise to win over Man Utd
Sports.content:
London City Lionesses started their star-studded era and the new season with a comfortable 2-1 win over Manchester United.

Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas made her debut for the club but despite the Spain international drawing a sell-out crowd at Hayes Lane, it was an own goal from Julia Zigiotti that opened the scoring.

The midfielder wrestled with Alanna Kennedy in the box before inadvertently guiding a header into the back of her own net to score the first goal of the 2026/27 campaign.

London City cruised into control of the fixture from there on, keeping United at arm's length throughout, before a moment of magic from Danielle van de Donk with a neat flick doubled the lead and sealed all three points for the hosts with under 10 minutes to go.

United substitute Simi Awujo tucked away a late consolation goal with virtually the last kick of the game and their only shot on target, highlighting the chasm in standards between the two sides with the talent London City now have at their disposal.

Rosa Kafaji, Mapi Leon, Putellas and Janni Thomsen were the fresh faces included and impressed - while Mary Earps and Kadidiatou Diani were unused on the bench - as an exciting new era got off to the perfect start while owner Michele Kang watched from the stands.

The key moments from Hayes Lane...

9: GOAL! Zigiotti's own goal gives London City the lead

49: SAVE! Kafaji forces a good save from Tullis-Joyce with a long-range shot

64: INJURY! Lucia Corrales goes off injured while clutching shoulder

82: SUPERB! Van den Donk's flick doubles London City's lead to seal three points

90+10: CONSOLATION! Awujo grabs late goal with United's only shot on target

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Simi Awujo smashes it home to grab a late goal for Manchester United against London City Lionesses.

Maestre: We were very dominant

London City Lionesses boss Eder Maestre:

"Starting with a win is very important to keep building confidence.

"I think we were very dominant through the whole game. I really think we deserved this win. I hope this kind of result makes the difference in the way we can keep playing in the next games we have.

"That's the identity we want - that's why I'm very proud of the team.

"Sometimes you need to take some risks to play in that way. The team played with the togetherness that I think are going to be the most important value to respect.

"I think we are one step closer to hitting the targets. I'm very excited and very happy."

'We were not us,' says Olid

Manchester United boss Eva Olid:

"I think none of us are happy with the first half. We were not us.

"Nothing that we have been working on was happening in the first half.

"In the half-time, it was me saying to them, this is not us, we need to have confidence, belief, show we want the ball, that has to be us.

"There was a change in the second half but at the end but I said at the end that needs to be 90 minutes. It's not enough just 40 minutes trying to have the ball."

Sports.title: 'Let's go one more time' - Taylor bows out from boxing at 'dream' venue
Sports.content:
Katie Taylor's glittering boxing career will draw to a close on Saturday night at her "dream venue" and with the message a simple one: "Let's go one more time".

Taylor will aim to retire as a three-time undisputed world champion when she takes on unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

The 40-year-old, who weighed in at 139.6lbs for the super-lightweight showdown compared to Pili's 139.9lbs, done it all in boxing.

Her accolades including winning Olympic gold in London in 2012 and, along with Amanda Serrano, becoming the first woman to headline a fight card at New York's iconic Madison Square ‌Garden.

She also avenged her sole pro defeat, against Chantelle Cameron.

But she has never fought at Croke Park before - until now.

Image: Pili (right) has a 12-0 record as a pro

'This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for'

While fight week, quite rightly, has seen the great and good of boxing and beyond praise Taylor's career, hail the inspiration she has been and discuss the legacy she will leave, the woman herself is not looking beyond Pili.

Speaking shortly after hitting the scales on Friday evening, the Bray Bomber, said: "My mind is focused on the fight. I have a job to do against a very tough challenger.

"I have built my reputation on always taking the tough fights, so why treat my last fight any differently? This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for. Let's go one more time."

Taylor did, though, turn to address her fans at the weigh-in, many of whom will also be rooting for her inside the stadium this weekend.

"I am blown away. I want to put on a performance worthy of the support I have had these last few years

"You guys have carried me throughout the Olympics and my whole career. Thank you so much. I am so grateful.

"I am so excited. I have been dreaming about this for the last few years and I am one day away from ending my career in a dream venue in front of all these amazing people."

Image: Katie Taylor has only lost once as a pro, a defeat to Chantelle Cameron that she went on to avenge

'Katie is an absolute hero to so many people'

Former world champion Carl Frampton, speaking on DAZN, feels the lure of a bout at Saturday's prolonged Taylor's time as an active fighter.

He said: "She has completed the sport but I think one of the reasons she held on was the dream of fighting at Croke Park. She has finally got it.

"Katie is an absolute hero to so many people, an inspiration. It is a perfect way to finish - but she has to win first and we can't rule out Pili who is a very good fighter."

But is it definitely it for Taylor - or is a return to the ring possible?

Three-weight world champion Mikaela Mayer added: "Katie has always been very true to her word.

"If she says this is her last fight, I believe it to be. If she wants to come back, I would not be upset about it. We'd love to see her again.

"I am benefitting off of her hard work and everything she has helped create for the women in this sport. I am sad as I had always hoped to share the ring with Katie."

Sports.title: 'It's going to be tight' - Hamilton eyes 'dream' Monza pole
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton is predicting a “very close” battle in Italian Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday for what he says would he says would be a “dream” pole position at Monza.

Hamilton was outperformed by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in both of Friday's practice sessions but the team's overall performance, following the arrival of a new engine upgrade, suggested they have the pace to compete for pole.

Leclerc topped Hamilton in first practice before Mercedes' George Russell was fastest in the second session, with Leclerc second and Hamilton only fifth behind Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.

Ferrari are set to go into qualifying, live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm, with a two-versus-one advantage over Mercedes due to world championship leader Kimi Antonelli having already incurred penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance that will see him start from the back of the grid regardless of where he finishes the session.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Italian Grand Prix.

"It's going to be tight, it's very close," Hamilton said. "We're up against the McLarens and the Mercedes, they are very, very competitive.

"Every weekend the Mercedes is just really, really quick. It'll be tough, for sure, but we need to knuckle down tonight and see if we can pull something out."

Asked about the possibility of starting on the front row or pole position at Ferrari's home race, Hamilton replied: "That's the dream, the ultimate dream.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number.

"Whether or not we can is the big, big question. And that's going to take a lot of work tonight to try to figure out if we've gone wrong anywhere and if there's any places we can improve, which there are loads of places we can improve.

"Also, I think being in the right place at the right time on track is going to help a lot."

Antonelli predicts 'tight fight' for pole

Despite not being a factor in the pole contest, Antonelli agrees with Hamilton's assessment that it will be a tight battle.

The 20-year-old Italian leads both Russell and Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with Norris trailing by 83 points in fourth.

Mercedes have chosen Antonelli's home race as the most suitable venue for him to serve an inevitable penalty for exceeding his engine allowance, due to a belief that fighting back through the field in Sunday's race will be easier at Monza than most other tracks that remain on this year's schedule.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli gives his thoughts on Ferrari after they debuted a new engine at the Italian GP practice sessions.

Antonelli said: "Today a bit of a different day compared to usual. A lot more focused on long runs so it was a bit weird, not going to lie, but overall, it was a good day.

"We gathered a lot of data and now looking forward to the next few days.

"Ferrari definitely took a step forward with a new engine and now the speeds are the same. We know how good their car is into the corners so, for sure, it's going to be a tight fight for pole tomorrow."

'Struggling' Norris doesn't expect to fight for pole

Norris arrived in Italy full of confidence having claimed back-to-back victories in Hungary and the Netherlands to reignite his hopes of defending his drivers' title.

However, the Brit was downcast after McLaren appeared unable to replicate their recent form at a track with very different characteristics to the previous two on the schedule.

Norris said: "Not very decent. Just struggling a lot more with pace.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A downbeat Lando Norris reflects on McLaren’s frustrating lack of pace in Friday Practice.

"In the corners we expected to be good at we're bad at and in the corners we expected to be bad at, we're not so bad at.

"But we're still off. So not in a great place at the minute. We'll see what we can do overnight but it's going to be tougher than before for sure.



"It's close between a lot of the guys at the top. The guys behind are not that far either so they can easily surprise us.

"I definitely don't feel we are in the fight for pole at all but we need to focus on getting a decent result."

Sports.title: Stella fumes at 'insulting' Briatore allegations after Alpine lose podium
Sports.content:
Andrea Stella has accused Alpine chief Flavio Briatore of "insulting" McLaren by questioning the relationship between the reigning constructors' champions and a judge at the FIA's International Court of Appeal.

The court announced on Friday that penalties given to Alpine driver Pierre Gasly during June's Monaco Grand Prix would be reinstated, following a successful appeal by McLaren and Red Bull.

Gasly took the chequered flag in third but was demoted when two five-second penalties for speeding in the pit lane were applied at that point. However, a right of review appeal from Alpine saw the penalties withdrawn five days later.

The reinstatement of the penalty drops Gasly back to seventh in the official classification. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar gets a podium in third, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri moves up to fourth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Isack Hadjar has been reinstated to the Monaco podium after a Red Bull appeal with Alpine expressing frustration as Pierre Gasly's penalty for speeding in pit lane is restored.

In an explosive press conference at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, which coincidentally featured Alpine executive director Briatore and McLaren team principal Stella, the pair engaged in a remarkable clash.

Alpine had put out a statement moments after the decision was announced expressing "disappointment" with the outcome but also said that the team "acknowledges the decision of the judging panel from the recent hearing in Paris".

Briatore stunned the room by striking a different tone in the press conference just a couple of hours later as he complained that one of the four judges at the hearing had a "working relationship" with McLaren.

"I think it's very unfair, firstly, but we accept the decision," Briatore said. "But what is very strange was the third judge in the panel, one of the judges acted like a prosecutor.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Red Bull Team Principal Laurent Mekies reacts to news that Isack Hadjar has been restored to third in the Monaco GP after Pierre Gasly’s two time penalties were reapplied.

"For this, not a big problem. The problem is, he is very linked with the McLaren company."

Briatore pointed to the individual's presence at a charity event in California in 2018, at which he claimed "two of three McLaren cars" were donated.

"We have a nice picture of this guy at the speech for McLaren in 2018," Briatore said.

"I think it was quite unfair that one of the judges was linked with a team protesting us."

Briatore added that the judge in question was "very nasty" to Alpine's representatives during the hearing, and said that his team were "thinking about" taking legal action.

The FIA has yet to formally respond to Briatore's comments but Sky Sports News understands the sport's governing body is confident in the independence of its International Court of Appeal and the process for selecting its panel of judges.

Sky Sports News also understands that McLaren consider they have no connection with the judge in question.

Stella: McLaren deserve a lot of respect

Stella initially chose not to respond to Briatore's comments, but eventually appeared to threaten his fellow Italian with legal action.

"I find that this conference is going in this direction quite insulting for McLaren, for the reputation of a team that deserves a lot of respect," Stella said.

"And if anybody makes this kind of allegations, which seem quite serious, they are going to have to take the responsibility for what they are saying in a public forum.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok explains why Pierre Gasly's Monaco GP penalties were previously overturned.

"The hearing, the whole international court of appeal was conducted to the highest standards. We should not question this space, like it's been done."

Stella has insisted throughout the process that McLaren were more interested in clarifying the rules for the good of the sport, rather than gaining two points for Piastri, who is not in championship contention this season.

"We had concerns which were beyond the fact that we might have lost two championship points, probably these two points aren't going to make any difference," Stella said.

"We were concerned about the application of sporting equality and fairness, and this is important. And this is not only important for McLaren.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri believes an 'awkward precedent' was set after Pierre Gasly's Monaco penalty was previously overturned.

"Not only Red Bull applied, but all teams were present in the hearing because this was a very important moment in terms of clarification as to how we apply the rules, as to how we apply consistency.

"And also, in this specific case, consistencies that are related to the methodologies that are valid throughout our race weekend."

Alpine won their right of review case after presenting evidence which the stewards agreed was a "significant and relevant new element" regarding an incorrect distance calculation in the pit lane, showing the Frenchman was in fact not speeding.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes' George Russell (whose penalty was later converted into a drive-through) and McLaren's Piastri were all hit by the same speeding sanction, but as the drivers had already served the penalties during the race they could not be undone.
