World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: Iraq, AIIB discuss financing development projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari met with a delegation from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) led by Konstantin Limitovskiy on Wednesday to discuss funding infrastructure and development projects in Iraq.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the AIIB delegation reviewed its global and regional portfolios to outline how its framework will apply to Iraq across the transportation, energy, water, and digital infrastructure sectors, according to a statement cited by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on the Development Road Project, Iraq’s mega-highway and rail corridor intended to connect the Gulf to Europe.

The AIIB publicly stated its willingness to fund and assist this important trans-regional corridor, acknowledging its enormous potential to drive economic diversification.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport held separate discussions with the World Bank and the AIIB to determine the technological integrations necessary for the project’s ports and rail networks.

The AIIB delegation expressed its willingness to assist and fund important projects in Iraq, particularly major infrastructure projects, such as the Development Road project, which would boost the country’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq launches plan to recover 100,000 artifacts smuggled abroad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has launched a comprehensive plan to recover over 100,000 artifacts that were unearthed through illegal excavation and smuggled out of the country.

The Iraqi Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities announced a broad endeavor to recover the country’s stolen Mesopotamian heritage using a combination of cultural diplomacy, security surveillance, and strong legal action.

The ministry’s undersecretary, Qasim al-Sudani, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the government’s agenda prioritizes the tourism sector.

The strategy emphasizes recovering documented items that were assigned official museum inventory numbers prior to their theft and smuggling, especially during the tumultuous period following the 2003 US-led invasion.

The initiative also seeks to tackle the significant number of unrecorded artifacts found during illegal and random excavations.

Since these items lack formal records, they pose a substantially more difficult legal issue to monitor and authenticate.

The Iraqi government has formed a combined domestic task force comprising the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the National Intelligence Service, and the National Security Service to carry out the plan.

Security agencies are cooperating with Iraqi embassies to identify stolen treasures that appear at public or private auctions abroad.

While countries like the United Kingdom and the United States have actively assisted in the return of tens of thousands of artifacts, Iraqi officials have indicated that some nations have intentionally delayed the repatriation process.

Iraq is also taking legal actions internationally against foreign businesses or individuals who are keeping Iraqi artifacts.

World.title: Iraq evaluates exploration blocks to optimize gas output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is actively assessing its exploration blocks and foreign alliances to maximize domestic gas output.

Director of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), Mohammed Yassin Hassan, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the ministry is focusing on unexploited exploration areas rather than existing resources.

The strategic measure seeks to attract multinational corporations to invest in Iraq’s growing natural gas sector.

Instead of altering production at current sites, the Oil Ministry is focusing on new exploration regions to identify new deposits.

Due to the strong interest in Iraq’s untapped energy potential, multinational energy businesses have already begun contacting the ministry.

Iraq’s MOC is actively pursuing partnerships with major US firms, such as ConocoPhillips, to lead gas development projects in important areas in the provinces of Diyala and Anbar.

Expanding operations in blocks such as the Akkas and Mansuriya gas fields is critical to Iraq’s long-term strategy for achieving energy independence and providing the necessary fuel for power plants to generate electricity.

World.title: Marsoumi: Iraq’s 10M bpd oil goal faces $75B cost and OPEC+ hurdles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s strategic plan to scale crude oil production to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030 faces formidable structural, financial, and geopolitical hurdles, prominent Iraqi economic analyst Dr. Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The assessment follows directives issued on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who instructed the Ministry of Oil to expand exploration licensing rounds and ramp up extraction across fields in federal territory and the Kurdistan Region to target nearly 10 million bpd over the next four years.

Al-Marsoumi outlined four primary structural constraints standing between Iraq’s current production baseline and the 10-million-bpd horizon:

OPEC+ Baseline & Quota Negotiation: Iraq currently produces approximately 4.431 million bpd against an OPEC+ baseline allocation of 4.651 million bpd. Pushing production toward 10 million bpd requires formal revision of Iraq’s sovereign quota—a concession requiring consensus among major OPEC+ members.

Sustainable Capacity Ceiling: US petroleum consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is actively auditing the maximum sustainable capacity across 19 OPEC+ nations. Preliminary assessments project Iraq’s sustainable 12-month ceiling at 5.0 to 5.5 million bpd, revealing a 4.5-million-bpd capacity deficit below the 2030 target.

Capital Expenditure Threshold ($75 Billion): Based on global industry benchmarks averaging $15 billion in capital investment per 1 million bpd of added capacity, Iraq must mobilize roughly $75 billion in upstream and midstream funding. This capital must finance seawater treatment and injection facilities, storage farm expansions, pumping stations, and new maritime and northern pipeline export corridors.

Price Collapse & Market Saturation Risks: Global oil absorption capacity remains constrained by demand growth projections. Injecting millions of additional Iraqi barrels risks igniting a market-share price war among producers, which could trigger a global oil price collapse harmful to Baghdad’s hydrocarbon-dependent treasury.

Comparative Analysis: Current Capacity vs. 2030 Target

Metric / Parameter Current Level (2026) 2030 Government Target Gap / Required Expansion Crude Output ~4.431 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +5.569 Million bpd Sustainable Ceiling 5.0 – 5.5 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +4.500 Million bpd OPEC+ Production Baseline 4.651 Million bpd Revised Allocation Required Requires OPEC+ Consensus Estimated Capital Outlay Baseline operational budget ~$75 Billion cumulative $15B per 1M bpd capacity Export Infrastructure Constrained southern/northern routes New northern & deepwater sea lines Major pipeline & storage expansion

Al-Marsoumi cautioned that upstream expansion cannot occur in isolation from global energy market fundamentals. Without substantial foreign direct investment to finance water injection schemes and deepwater export berths, aggressive target-setting risks outpacing actual midstream logistics.

Furthermore, aggressively pursuing volume over price discipline could depress international crude benchmarks, reducing net state oil revenues even as export volumes increase.

World.title: SC awards pension to Mumbai engineer who forged ST certificate
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has rewarded a wrongdoer - a man who got appointed as a junior civil engineer in Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) by producing a forged ST certificate, and, subsequently, stalled the scrutiny of his eligibility for quota for more than a decade - by allowing him to superannuate in peace with retirement benefits.

Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community. Based on the certificate, he was appointed a junior civil engineer in MCGM in 1994. He misplaced the original ST certificate but managed to secure a fresh one from the sub-divisional magistrate, Bhusawal division, in Oct 2000.

Following scrutiny initiated by MCGM, the Police Vigilance Cell traced Patil's family history and found that his ancestors had been recorded as 'Koli', 'Hindu Koli' and 'Hindu Suryawanshi Koli', none of which belonged to the ST category.

In July 2009, MCGM issued a show cause notice to Patil.

He successfully dodged and delayed proceedings before the scrutiny committee until Jan 2020, when the panel rejected his plea that his lawyer and elderly family members were not available, and invalidated the ST certificate. HC dismissed his appeal against cancellation of ST status.

SC, however, stayed Patil's dismissal from service through an interim order on Nov 18, 2021.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi Thursday upheld the cancellation of Patil's ST certificate and Bombay HC order. However, it took a lenient view given his undertaking that he or any of his family members "shall (not) be entitled to claim any future benefit on the basis of the invalidated ST certificate".

The ruling contrasts with SC's consistent rulings against benefits accruing to people who forge SC or ST certificates to gain admission or employment.

World.title: HC allows 2 'linked' to NEET leak to go for counselling
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has directed National Testing Agency (NTA) to declare within 24 hours the NEET-UG re-examination results of two candidates, whose results were withheld over allegations linking them to the question paper leak.

Justice Jasmeet Singh pointed out the candidates had not been named as accused by CBI in its chargesheet.

While CBI told the court that it did not make them accused, though they had paid money to get question papers, the judge observed that at this stage, it was just an allegation and "therefore, the petitioners cannot be treated as persons against whom criminal culpability has been established or as having been found guilty of any illegality".

The court was hearing the students' plea seeking release of their re-NEET results and permission to participate in the ongoing counselling. The CBI chargesheet named the two petitioners as witnesses, and not accused. NTA, however, issued show-cause notices to them and withheld their results.

During the hearing, NTA submitted that it withheld the results after CBI informed it that several candidates had allegedly received or shared the question paper of the May 3 examination.





On its part, CBI submitted that the petitioners had received the question paper and had the "mens rea" (intent) to commit the illegality, since money had been paid by them for obtaining the question paper.

HC observed that the petitioners were at a "nascent stage of their academic careers", and withholding their results merely on the basis of allegations that were yet to be tested would cause serious prejudice to them.

World.title: Smoking raises mortality risk by 55% for diabetics
World.content:
Smoking raises mortality risk by 55% for diabetics

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type-2 diabetes care. Experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-ups instead of being given a one-time "quit smoking" warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, represent the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type-2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses to people with diabetes.A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of their quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetics, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type-2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quitting strategies and relapse prevention.

World.title: PMLA court: Cheques, drugs constitute proceeds of crime
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Broadening the definition of "property" under Prevention of Money Laundering Act, a special PMLA court in Mohali has ruled that seized bank cheques, even if not encashed, and narcotics both fall under the definition of "property" and constitute proceeds of crime under the money laundering Act.

The judgement came Thursday, when ED launched a massive search operation at 30 premises across all zones of the southern region in different narcotics-related cases. The searches are being conducted under the mandate of Centre's 'Nasha Mukt Bharat' campaign with targets in the first phase spread across Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

The judge convicted two accused and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years, while rejecting the contention of the defence that their property and bank accounts were not attached and the seized contraband could not be considered proceeds of crime as no money trail had been brought on the record.

Special judge Hardip Singh also rejected the defence's argument that the cheques recovered from the accused were not encashed and thus could not constitute proceeds of crime. The judge noted that the cheques were exchanged for the purpose of purchasing the contraband and the accused could not provide any explanation to the contrary.

Starting with the four southern states, ED Thursday began a crackdown on major drug syndicates operating across the country.





The drive has been launched as part of Centre's "drug-free India" campaign to attach properties of all those engaged in drug dealing and generation of "proceeds of crime". The ED's search covered targets involved in trafficking of illicit drugs like methamphetamine, marijuana, and MDMA.

Over 20 foreign nationals are under scanner, an official said.

Searches were conducted at premises in Chennai, Tirunelveli, Nagapattinam, Velankanni and Ramanathapuram in Tamil Nadu; Kolar, Malur (Kolar district) and Hoskote (Bengaluru North district); Serilingampally and Nanakramguda (Hyderabad) and Ranga Reddy district in Telangana; Kozhikode, Kannur, Malappuram and Thrissur in Kerala.

ED is coordinating with other central agencies and state police forces that have registered cases of

in the past few years to further investigate the money trail and track the proceeds of crime.

"The investigation prima facie discloses not merely trafficking of methamphetamine, but also the generation, receipt and movement of money arising out of this," a senior official said, adding that syndicates were using hawala and crypto currency dealers to further transfer the proceeds of crime outside the country to tax havens.

World.title: India working with Moscow, Kyiv to end war: EAM

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said Friday India is exploring ideas with both Russia and Ukraine to bring the conflict to an end, while again defending India's energy sourcing and underlining that it's important to "diagnose" the problem right. The minister had said in Ukraine a day ago that the conflict will end through dialogue and diplomacy and not oil trade.Without revealing if there was any specific peace proposal under consideration, Jaishankar said India was having "detailed discussions" with both sides about possible ways to facilitate peace. He was speaking in Warsaw after a meeting with his Polish counterpart Radoslaw Sikorski."PM Modi and President Putin met in Bishkek three days ago, and then I went to Kyiv. So, what we had were discussions with the Russian side, yesterday with the Ukrainian side, and what we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they would contribute to the mitigation, ideally the cessation of the conflict," he said.India has so far not come up with a plan of its own to ensure a ceasefire as it believes the primary responsibility to end the war lies with Russia and Ukraine.However, as Jaishankar reiterated, it's ready to offer any assistance, if required, to ensure peace.After Modi's renewed peace message to Putin, there seems to be more urgency in India's efforts, with Jaishankar calling on Zelensky and discussing "approaches to end the ongoing conflict"." ...We must each do what we can, in whichever way we believe would be most effective. And support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is India's strong conviction, and we are acting on it," Jaishankar said in Poland. "I think let's diagnose the problem right. The issue is a conflict, and the solution to that is not in trade. The solution... is in negotiations."

World.title: RSS says of critics of Mohan Bhagwat’s UK trip: ‘Let them speak, we’re open to dialogue’
World.content:
RSS spokesman Sunil Ambekar in London for Mohan Bhagwat visit

LONDON: The RSS shrugged off criticism by civil groups of its chief Dr Mohan Bhagwatâs UK trip, saying in a democracy differences of opinions are expected and âshould not be taken as a shockâ.The RSS head arrived in London on Sept 2 on the final leg of his three-city outreach RSS centenary tour, having just visited New York and Toronto on a âdialogue mission.âHindus for Human Rights UK and several other campaign groups wrote an open letter to London mayor Sadiq Khan asking him to condemn the visit, pointing out New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani had done that.Labour PIO MP Nadia Whittome tabled a written parliamentary question asking the home office whether âthe visit engages the commitment to block hate preachers and extremists from entering the UKâ.âWe are here for peace, integration and oneness and we are open for dialogue with everyone. In a democracy, it is very normal to raise different voices. We are engaging with those who wish to dialogue with us,â RSS head of media Sunil Ambekar said at a press briefing on Friday.âWe are here to communicate what we are and how we think. We are very much open. We have nothing to hide. We expect a debate and exchange of thoughts. Let them speak.âOn allegations the RSS was behind the 2022 Leicester riots, Ambekar said this was a âUK domestic issueâ. âThere is no questionâ¦ RSS was not involved. Already people are finding out their legal options. Hindus are a peace-loving community.âHe said there are a lot of âmisconceptionsâ in the West. âBharat is not a nation state political concept â it is a cultural concept. Hindutva is not like any religion â itâs a concept where there will be respect for all religious practices. That is Hindutva, and that is Bharat, so I think the trip will help to clear the ideas,â he said.A spokesperson for the London mayor said the mayor âdoes not have the powerâ to ban people from speaking. âLondon is proud to celebrate our diversity and intolerance has no place in our great city,â the spokesperson said.

World.title: Terrorist shot dead in J&K’s Budgam
World.content:
Security forces Friday gunned down a terrorist during an anti-terror operation deep inside a forest area

SRINAGAR: Security forces Friday gunned down a terrorist during an anti-terror operation deep inside a forest area in J&Kâs Budgam district, about 60km from Srinagar, the Army stated.Based on intelligence inputs, a joint team of the Army, J&K Police and CRPF launched a search operation in Budgamâs Ashdar Gali area, the Armyâs Srinagar-based Chinar Corps stated in an X post.Holed-up ultras opened fire at the search party, triggering a fierce gunfight in which one terrorist was shot dead.
